items.title: U2 to Be Honored as 2027 MusiCares Persons of the Year
items.summary:
MusiCares has named U2 its 2027 Persons of the Year, honoring Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr. at the organization's 36th annual benefit gala. Billboard reported the ceremony will take place Friday, Feb. 5, 2027, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, two nights ahead of the Grammy Awards at Crypto.com Arena.

U2 becomes the fourth band to take the honor, after Fleetwood Mac in 2018, Aerosmith in 2020 and the Grateful Dead in 2025. Bono was recognized on his own at the 2003 gala, which makes him the first honoree to be cited both individually and as part of a group. The band has won 22 Grammys, more than any other group or duo, and remains the only act to win twice in each of the album, record and song of the year categories.

In a joint statement, the band pointed to the crews and collaborators behind five decades of records and tours. "We've been recording and touring for 50 years because of that pool, from producers and engineers to carpenters and riggers," the members said, adding that they were "very excited to be in the front row of our first ever U2 gig…we know we're gonna be outplayed."

Recording Academy and MusiCares CEO Harvey Mason jr. framed the selection around the band's charitable work as much as its catalog. "Their impact goes far beyond the stage," he said in a statement. The four members met at a Dublin high school in 1976 and campaigned against apartheid in South Africa before signing a record deal; Amnesty International gave them its Ambassador of Conscience Award in 2005.

Individually, Bono co-founded ONE and (RED) and pressed President George W. Bush to establish PEPFAR. The Edge co-founded Music Rising after Hurricane Katrina to replace instruments lost in disasters, Clayton has spoken publicly about addiction recovery and received the MusiCares Stevie Ray Vaughan Award in 2017, and Mullen Jr. produced the dyslexia documentary Left Behind. The band has also funded Music Generation, Ireland's national music education program.

The gala moves from the Los Angeles Convention Center to the Peacock Theater, which seats roughly 7,100, and MusiCares is selling individual theater seats for the tribute concert alongside the usual dinner tables. Lewis & Clark, the live event outfit run by Joe Lewis and R.A. Clark, produces again. Proceeds support MusiCares programs covering health services, addiction recovery, mental health, disaster relief and financial assistance for music professionals.

items.title: Snoop Dogg to Host 2026 MTV VMAs
items.summary:
Snoop Dogg will host the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, which return to California for the first time since 2017. Billboard reported the show airs live coast-to-coast from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Sunday, Sept. 27, from 7:30 to 9:30 p.m. ET on CBS, simulcast on MTV and streaming on Paramount+ Premium, with global availability on Paramount+ and MTV the following day.

The Long Beach native is a 13-time VMAs nominee with three wins, and his history with the show goes back to a 1994 main stage debut performing "Murder Was the Case." He later teamed with Dr. Dre and Eminem to close the 1999 show, paid tribute to The Notorious B.I.G. alongside Diddy in 2005, and performed with Eminem in 2022 in a segment built around the Otherside metaverse.

"MTV and the VMAs have been part of my story since the beginning," Snoop said in a statement. "They gave hip-hop a place to be loud, fearless and seen by the whole world." He singled out producer Van Toffler, who worked at MTV during Snoop's early years there: "Now we get to make some new history."

The booking continues two patterns at the show. Snoop is the sixth consecutive hip-hop artist to host, following Doja Cat in 2021, Jack Harlow with LL Cool J and Nicki Minaj in 2022, Minaj alone in 2023, Megan Thee Stallion in 2024 and LL Cool J last year. At 54, he is also the second host in a row over 50, after LL hosted at 57.

MTV is leaning on legacy acts elsewhere on the card. The network announced on Sept. 9 that Nirvana will receive this year's Video Vanguard Award, and Madonna leads the nominations. Snoop and Nirvana both won at the 1994 ceremony, hosted by Roseanne Barr, with Snoop taking best rap video for "Doggy Doggy World" and Nirvana best alternative video for "Heart-Shaped Box."

Gunpowder & Sky produces the telecast, with Toffler as producer and Jesse Ignjatovic, Barb Bialkowski, Bruce Gillmer, Barry Barclay and Floris Bauer as executive producers. Snoop Dogg also serves as an executive producer. MTV will announce performers, presenters and guests in the coming weeks.

items.title: Gaza Doc ‘NAZA,’ From ‘No Other Land’ Directors, Earns Record-Breaking 24.5-Minute Venice Ovation as Producer Jonathan Glazer Leads Applause
items.summary:
NAZA, a documentary from No Other Land directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, drew a 24.5-minute standing ovation at its Venice Film Festival premiere on Thursday. Variety reported it is the longest ovation in the festival's history, surpassing the 22 minutes given last year to The Voice of Hind Rajab, and apparently the longest recorded at any film festival.

Jonathan Glazer, who directed The Zone of Interest and executive produced NAZA, embraced both directors and cheered through the applause. Abraham and Szor were visibly emotional, wiping their eyes as audience members raised Palestinian flags in the theater.

The film was shot at night on rooftops in Tel Aviv and is built around interviews with 24 Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers. Its official synopsis says it details the systems behind Israel's mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza. The title comes from an acronym used by Israeli intelligence for the number of civilians expected to be killed in an airstrike.

Abraham and Szor were two of the four directors behind No Other Land, which won the Academy Award for best documentary in 2025 and followed Israeli efforts to displace Palestinians in the southern West Bank. Speaking to Variety before the premiere, Abraham said the pair wanted to use their access "to people in our own society who went into the military to look at that system as it carried out what all human rights organizations are saying is a genocide."

The Guardian and James Wilson of JW Films produced NAZA, reuniting Wilson and Glazer, who won an Oscar together for The Zone of Interest. It is the only documentary feature in this year's Venice competition. Kaouther Ben Hania, whose The Voice of Hind Rajab set the previous ovation record, sits on the jury led by Maggie Gyllenhaal that names the winners Saturday.

items.title: Nice As Fuck Announce Reunion Tour
items.summary:
Nice As Fuck, the trio of Jenny Lewis, Au Revoir Simone's Erika Forster and the Like's Tennessee Thomas, have announced a reunion tour, a decade after the group's only album. Stereogum reported the band will play a short run of club shows in October, with DJ Alix Brown opening, alongside a reissue of the self-titled record.

The group came together in 2016 and played its first show at a Bernie Sanders benefit before surprise-releasing its debut a few months later. A tour and a performance on Colbert followed, and then the project stopped. The new dates mark the album's 10th anniversary.

The eight-show run begins Oct. 16 at Sid the Cat in Pasadena and continues to San Francisco's August Hall, Nectar Lounge in Seattle, Portland's Wonder Ballroom, Outset in Chicago, the Black Cat in Washington, D.C., and Philadelphia's Theatre of the Living Arts, closing Oct. 29 at Xanadu Roller Arts in Brooklyn.

Lewis has spent recent months on a Rilo Kiley reunion, and Thomas got married last month. Tickets for the Nice As Fuck shows are on sale now, and the reissue is available to pre-order.

items.title: Julien Baker Returns to the Road With Rock Club Residency Tour This Fall
items.summary:
Julien Baker will return to touring this fall with a run of three-night residencies in six cities, her first extended stretch of live shows since boygenius finished touring in 2024. Rolling Stone reported the month-long rock club tour opens Oct. 15 at Kilby Court in Salt Lake City and ends Nov. 21 at Neumos in Seattle.

Between those bookends, Baker plays three nights each at the Middle East in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Cat's Cradle in Carrboro, North Carolina, the 40 Watt in Athens, Georgia, and the Bottleneck in Lawrence, Kansas. Ticket details are on her website.

The announcement came a day after Baker played an unannounced show Wednesday at the Blue Room in Nashville, backed by longtime collaborators Matt Gilman and Calvin Lauber. Both will join her for the residencies. At that show she played material from her solo catalog and debuted four new songs, described in a press release as music that came out of recent studio time.

Baker had stepped away from performing after canceling a planned summer 2025 tour supporting her joint album with Torres, citing her well-being and a need to focus on her health. She began easing back in late August with a solo show in Nantucket, Massachusetts, and turned up as a surprise guest at boygenius bandmate Lucy Dacus' Outside Lands set.

Her most recent solo album, Little Oblivions, came out in 2021.
